question: Expose Leon over HTTP
expected:
<!--
Thanks for your interest in Leon! ❤️
Please check if there is no similar issue before creating this one.
-->

### Feature Use Case

- Request specific modules actions on demand over HTTP.
- Much better support of third-party clients (Discord, Signal, Telegram, Messenger, etc.) thanks to the HTTP protocol. So we could talk with Leon and ask him to do things from these third-party clients.

### Feature Proposal

#### 1. We can automatically expose Leon modules actions to a HTTP API:

As every package contains JSON configuration, more specifically the `expressions/{LANG}.json`, it can be parsed to expose an HTTP endpoint/route for each module action.
E.g. from the To-Do List module that belongs to the Calendar package:
```json
"create_list": {
  "expressions": [
    "Create the x list",
    "Create a x list"
  ],
  "entities": [
    {
      "type": "trim",
      "name": "list",
      "conditions": [
        {
          "type": "between",
          "from": ["the", "a", "an", "my"],
          "to": ["list", "list", "list", "list"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Can be translated to:
```bash
# {HTTP METHOD} /api/p/{PACKAGE}/{MODULE}/{ACTION}
POST /api/p/calendar/todolist/create_list
```
`p` for "package" to scope the sub routes so we don't have any conflict with other parent routes we may have in the future.
We can consider `entities` as body parameters for the HTTP request. Here, `list` would be one body data.

Every endpoint will be reachable via a `POST` or a `GET` HTTP method by default (if there are any params/entities, then it will be `POST`, otherwise it will be `GET`). However, an option `http_api.method` in the expressions JSON files may be added for each action so it can define a specific HTTP method.

A `http_api.timeout` option can be set for each action/route to set a timeout and returns a timeout error earlier.
A `http_api.disabled` with a `true` can be set to explicitly disable a specific action to be available over HTTP.

From the `.env` file, a `LEON_OVER_HTTP` environment variable will be available to enable or disable this feature. It will be enabled by default.

In case of built-in entities, such as domain name, date range, etc. Entities need to be explicitly written in a package configuration at the action level to allow actions to be supported over HTTP.
E.g. from the Is It Down module:
```json
"http_api": {
  "entities": [
    {
      "entity": "url",
      "resolution": [
        "value"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Which will allow such request:
```bash
POST http://localhost:1337/api/p/checker/isitdown/run
{
    "url": [{ "value": "github.com" }, { "value": "twitch.tv" }]
}
```

#### 2. Expose queries over HTTP:

An endpoint such as `POST /api/core/query` with a `query` body parameter can be exposed so Leon can go through his understanding logic before executing an action and then return the HTTP response according to the action response.

A `http_api.timeout` option can be set for each action/route to set a timeout and returns a timeout error earlier.

question: "Modules" to "skills" new structure
expected:
<!--
Thanks for your interest in Leon! ❤️
Please check if there is no similar issue before creating this one.
-->

### Expected Behavior

Complete new modules structure and transition from "modules" to "skills".

### Actual Behavior

The current modules structure depends on modules developers and the whole structure isn't scalable enough.

### Proposal

As Leon plans to grow, I believe that having a specific folders/files structure is essential.
Mainly the following reasons make me think like this:

- At the moment, Leon skills are developed in Python only. Soon, the JavaScript bridge will come so it'll be possible to develop skills using JavaScript too. So having a hierarchy between bridges will help to be consistent between every module.
- Some skills are small, some will be bigger. Some skills will require more business logic than others, so it is crucial to define a well organized and scalable structure.

Also, when we get to know about Leon, "modules" can means everything, it is too abstract. I think "skills" is more appropriate as it really means something and we may be more familiar with this word.

Leon NLP will be improved so we can build more powerful skills. Hence, a transition needs to be made from "packages" to "domains". These domains need to be defined, so skills developers don't need to create one, but just put their skills in the corresponding domain. Doing so will allow a better NLU accuracy.

- More details can be found in [this roadmap card](https://trello.com/c/SQl06isp/415-%F0%9F%94%A7-100-beta7-new-modules-to-skills-structure).
- The development can be followed via [this branch](https://github.com/leon-ai/leon/tree/from-modules-to-skills).
